pages.title: Colony-keepers
text: “You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it.”

pages.title: Who they are
text: The Colony-keepers routed Pulse through the comb and planted the March flowers for their swarms. Take without asking and the comb goes quiet. Their craft is **hives and March flowers**.
Their camps stand in **flower forests**, meadows and cherry groves, and a second camp keeps the old road on the March steppe.

pages.title: What they want
text: Their reagent is the **Lantern Down**, worth **+8** standing at their hearth.
They also favour a Honey Bottle, Honeycomb, a Honey Block or any flower: **+3** each. Any other food is worth **+1**, and a charged Pulse Cell **+2 for every 10 Pulse**, up to +8.
Remember the hearth takes at most **60** standing a day from offerings; see [Tribes and standing](standing).

pages.title: What the Elder trades
text: **Guest**: 4 Honeycomb for 2 Echo Shards; 2 Honey Bottles for 2 Ley Thistles.
**Friend**: 8 Honeycomb for 2 Echo Blooms; 2 Honey Blocks for a Lantern Down.
**Kin**: 4 Attuned Echo for a Ley Collector; 2 Bound Echo for 3 Spiritweave.

pages.title: Their Mark and totem
text: At **Voice** the Elder gives you the Colony-keepers' Tribe Mark. Craft it with a {item:tribalpower:resonance_totem_air} and two Spiritweave into their [Kinship Totem](kinship_totem).
Beside a Pulse Resonator it is one more voice; beside a station it lends **Air**.
Their Kin trade for Spiritweave is handy: every Kinship Totem needs two.
Kin of the Colony-keepers carry their [boon](tribe_boons): bees never turn on you.
